stops.note: to stretch forth, to claim falsely, from prae- (before) and tendere (to stretch)
stops.meaning: to stretch forth, to claim falsely

stops.note: settled as the English word for acting as if something is true when it isn't
stops.meaning: to act as if something is true when it is not

current_meaning: to act as if something is the case when it is not, especially in play or deception
